name: consumer_atom_layer_review
objective: Review one product idea against the owner's consumer-psychology atom dictionary (8 layers L0-L7, 75 atomic factors, 7 moderators): mark which atoms the idea activates, record mechanism, indicator, behavior effect and moderators with the evidence behind each, critique every layer, chain the activated atoms into a causal path and name the validation tasks. The final deliverable is an Excel workbook built from the committed artifacts by scripts/consumer_atom_review_xlsx.py. The source model is an integrating framework, not a validated standard. v1.1 (owner's sample sheet, 2026-10-15): free text in the language of the request (ko or en, Korean when unstated; compiler-checked); each activated atom also carries a numeric score (1-5, capped by the evidence grade), a testable hypothesis and an improvement recommendation; the verdict adds the idea summary, value boxes, ratings, a judgment limited by the recorded evidence, an action plan and additional notes; the workbook follows the single-sheet layout of the sample.
rules: Every atom of the dictionary is answered once and every claim cites evidence or is an assumption
Layer, name and meaning of an atom and its evidence grade are derived by the compiler, never written by the model
Confidence cannot exceed the ceiling of the evidence grade
Moderators are kept apart from atoms: they are listed per atom, never counted as atoms
The per-layer table and the evidence status are computed by the compiler; hypothesis_only never means the idea will fail or sell

steps.description: Restate the idea as product, customer and situation using only words from the idea statement.
steps.instruction: The idea is in the intent between IDEA_JSON_BEGIN and IDEA_JSON_END and the evidence rows between EVIDENCE_JSON_BEGIN and EVIDENCE_JSON_END. Write `product`, `customer` and `situation`, each as {text, quote}: `text` is a short phrase and `quote` is copied word for word from the idea statement. Do not add facts the statement does not contain. Language: if the intent holds a LANGUAGE_JSON block {id: output, code}, write EVERY free-text field in that language (ko = Korean, en = English); without the block write Korean (한국어). The compiler checks the script of each text. Evidence quotes are the only exception: they stay word for word in the language of the evidence row (the INTAKE quotes in the language of the idea statement); do not translate them. Fixed values (relevance, direction, behavior_effect, moderators, final_judgment, ratings) keep their listed words.

steps.description: Review the idea against the 29 atoms of layers L0, L1, L2, L3.
steps.instruction:
The idea is in the intent between IDEA_JSON_BEGIN and IDEA_JSON_END and the evidence rows between EVIDENCE_JSON_BEGIN and EVIDENCE_JSON_END (each row has id, kind and text; kind is one of assumption, statement, behavior, payment, repeat_outcome). For EVERY atom listed below write exactly one record in `atoms`. relevance: activated = the idea touches or depends on this atom in the purchase path; inactive = it plays no role (say why in claim); unknown = the idea gives no way to tell (say what is missing). `evidence` is a list of {id, quote} with the quote copied word for word from that evidence row, or an empty list when the claim is only an assumption; the compiler derives the evidence grade from the row kind and caps `score` (1-5) by it (an activated record's `score`: E0 at most 2, E1 at most 3, E2 at most 4, E3 and above 5). Activated records also need: score (integer 1-5 = how strongly the idea handles this atom in a way the evidence supports; 1 very weak, 5 very strong), hypothesis (the testable statement to verify, 12+ characters), recommendation (the improvement you advise, 12+ characters), direction (supports | hinders | mixed = effect of the idea on purchase through this atom), precondition (when the atom is activated), mechanism (what it changes), indicator (how it could be measured), behavior_effect (a list from ['purchase', 'hold', 'churn']: purchase, hold, churn) and moderators (a list from {'M1': '개인차', 'M2': '문화·집단', 'M3': '제품 관여도', 'M4': '구매 맥락', 'M5': '시간 지평', 'M6': '자원 제약', 'M7': '기존 경험'}, empty when none applies). Inactive and unknown records carry only id, relevance, claim, evidence, critique. critique is your review of the risks and counter-arguments around this atom (a sentence of 20+ characters for activated records, 12+ otherwise). Use only the evidence rows; a claim without a cited row is an assumption. Language: if the intent holds a LANGUAGE_JSON block {id: output, code}, write EVERY free-text field in that language (ko = Korean, en = English); without the block write Korean (한국어). The compiler checks the script of each text. Evidence quotes are the only exception: they stay word for word in the language of the evidence row (the INTAKE quotes in the language of the idea statement); do not translate them. Fixed values (relevance, direction, behavior_effect, moderators, final_judgment, ratings) keep their listed words.

steps.description: Critique each of the 8 layers and chain the activated atoms into a causal path to behavior.
steps.instruction: Write `layers`: one record per layer L0..L7, each exactly {layer, critique, weakest_atom}. critique (40+ characters) reviews how the idea handles that layer as a whole; weakest_atom is the id of the activated atom of that layer the idea handles worst, or exactly none when no atom of the layer is activated. Write `chain`: at least 3 edges {from, to, why} between ATOMS you activated, showing the causal path through which the idea could lead to purchase (why is 20+ characters). The source text says the order is not fixed: an edge may run backwards (for example from learning after use to memory or self) when that is what happens. Language: if the intent holds a LANGUAGE_JSON block {id: output, code}, write EVERY free-text field in that language (ko = Korean, en = English); without the block write Korean (한국어). The compiler checks the script of each text. Evidence quotes are the only exception: they stay word for word in the language of the evidence row (the INTAKE quotes in the language of the idea statement); do not translate them. Fixed values (relevance, direction, behavior_effect, moderators, final_judgment, ratings) keep their listed words.

steps.description: Closing critique: strengths, risks and the three validation tasks. The compiler writes the per-layer table and the evidence status.
steps.instruction: Write `overall` (60+ characters, your critique of the whole idea), `strongest` (at most 5 activated atoms whose direction is supports), `top_risks` (records {atom_id, why}: include EVERY activated atom whose direction is hinders, plus others that worry you most, at most 8 unless more atoms hinder) and `validation_plan`: exactly one record for each task of ['causal_separation', 'time_measurement', 'individual_mechanism'] (causal_separation = separate cause from selection, time_measurement = measure before, during and after use, individual_mechanism = estimate which path works for which consumer), each {task, atom_ids, design} with at least one activated atom and a design sentence of 30+ characters. The compiler adds layer_table and evidence_status; never write them yourself. Language: if the intent holds a LANGUAGE_JSON block {id: output, code}, write EVERY free-text field in that language (ko = Korean, en = English); without the block write Korean (한국어). The compiler checks the script of each text. Evidence quotes are the only exception: they stay word for word in the language of the evidence row (the INTAKE quotes in the language of the idea statement); do not translate them. Fixed values (relevance, direction, behavior_effect, moderators, final_judgment, ratings) keep their listed words. Also write: idea_name (short name), problem (20+ characters), core_hypothesis (the core consumer-psychology hypothesis, 20+), functional_value, emotional_value, self_value (12+ each: what the idea gives on the functional, emotional and identity side), biggest_uncertainty (12+), priority_experiment (20+), ratings {potential, feasibility, appeal} each one of 높음 | 보통 | 낮음, final_judgment (one of 진행 | 조건부 진행 | 보류 | 중단; the compiler limits it: 진행 needs at least half of the activated atoms at grade E3 or above, 중단 needs at least two hindering atoms backed by grade E2 or above), judgment_reason (30+), action_plan (3-6 items {priority 1..n in order, action, detail 20+, owner (a team or role), duration, atom_ids (activated atoms)}) and additional_notes (2-6 sentences). The compiler adds mean scores per layer, overall_mean_score, completed_share and allowed_judgments; never write them yourself.
